methodological_rigor.justification: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial with stratified randomization (liver metastases, prior chemoradiotherapy, ECOG status) strengthens internal validity. 63.5-month median follow-up provides mature OS data (68% maturity). Cox proportional hazards models with stratified log-rank tests appropriately applied. Proportional hazards assumption tested (Grambsch-Therneau test, Schoenfeld residuals). Age imbalance identified and multivariable adjustment performed post hoc (HR 0.65). Subgroup analyses examined consistency.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Randomized controlled trial (1b) with high clinical relevance: first 5-year OS evidence for PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in RM-NPC. Demonstrates 13.6% absolute OS benefit (37.8% vs 24.2% at 5 years), establishing new benchmark for standard-of-care. Direct impact on clinical practice for large patient population in endemic regions. EBV DNA clearance as biomarker has immediate clinical application.

reporting_quality.justification: Well-reported RCT with CONSORT diagram, balanced baseline characteristics (except age), clearly defined primary/secondary endpoints. Comprehensive safety and efficacy reporting. Extended follow-up (5 years) with mature OS data. Subgroup and exploratory analyses appropriately labeled. Limitations section acknowledges geographic restriction (endemic Asia), survivorship bias, and lack of multiplicity adjustment. Data from multicenter trial, access presumably restricted to approved collaborators.

novelty_literature.justification: Secondary analysis of CAPTAIN-1st trial with novel 5-year follow-up perspective. PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy for RM-NPC is established approach (5 major trials conducted 2018-2024), but extended 5-year OS data is new. EBV DNA dynamics as prognostic biomarker extends prior work. Meaningful contribution to understanding durability of immune checkpoint inhibitor benefit but builds on known therapeutic strategy.

writing_presentation.justification: Excellent clarity and organization. Methods clearly describe randomization, stratification, and statistical approach. Results section logically presents OS, EBV dynamics, and subgroup analyses. Kaplan-Meier curves effectively communicate survival differences. Discussion appropriately contextualizes 5-year landmark and survival plateau phenomenon in immunotherapy. Limitations section transparent about geographic restriction and potential biases.

key_strengths: First 5-year OS evidence for PD-1 inhibitor in RM-NPC: 37.8% vs 24.2%, with 13.6% absolute benefit and adjusted HR 0.65
Rigorous RCT design with double-blind, placebo-controlled methodology and stratified randomization
Mature follow-up (63.5 months median, 68% OS maturity) supports durability claims and survival plateau observation
Novel biomarker finding: rapid EBV DNA clearance (within 3 cycles) strongly predicts long-term survival (46.8% vs 7.5% 5-year OS)
Comprehensive subgroup analyses demonstrating consistent OS benefits across age, ECOG status, and metastatic site
key_concerns: Geographic limitation: enrollment restricted to NPC-endemic East Asian regions; generalizability to Western populations with keratinizing histology unknown
Post hoc age-adjusted analysis due to baseline imbalance (56% vs 43% aged ≥50 years); adjustment was not prespecified
Secondary endpoint (OS) analyzed without multiplicity adjustment; borderline P=.047 unadjusted (P=.006 adjusted)
Survivorship bias acknowledged: patients completing 2 years camrelizumab had 87.1% 5-year OS vs 18.9% with early discontinuation; unclear if causality or selection effect
Loss to follow-up: 9 (6.7%) camrelizumab and 12 (9.3%) placebo patients; potential impact on long-term outcomes unclear
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality RCT with mature 5-year OS data establishing clinically meaningful benefit of camrelizumab plus chemotherapy in RM-NPC. Double-blind, placebo-controlled design and discovery of EBV DNA clearance as prognostic biomarker strengthen contribution. Fits Tier 1 criteria (strong novelty as first 5-year evidence, rigorous design, direct clinical significance). Geographic limitation requires validation in non-endemic populations but does not diminish quality of current evidence.
